extracted.intended_audience: Hospitals participating in or considering participation in the CJR‑X model, their clinical/administrative/compliance staff, SNFs, and other provider stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory requirements and conditions for CJR‑X model participation covering telehealth waivers, the SNF 3‑day stay waiver and beneficiary protections, and sharing of beneficiary‑identifiable claims data with participating hospitals. Focused on operational, coverage, billing, quality, monitoring, privacy, and data sharing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of auxiliary licensed clinical staff for high-level home telehealth visits
rubrics_metrics.description: If a high-level (level 4 or 5) home telehealth visit is not contemporaneous with a home nursing visit or during an authorized period of home health care, require the physician to document in the medical record that auxiliary licensed clinical staff were available on site in the patient's home during the visit and if they were not, to document the reason that such a high-level visit would not require such personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes either billing the visit on the same claim with the same date of service as a home nursing visit or during an authorized home health care period, or else the physician must explicitly document presence of auxiliary staff or explain why auxiliary staff were not needed for the specific visit. CMS will monitor compliance with this documentation requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home telehealth E/M services follow standard Medicare E/M coverage/payment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Services described by the proposed home telehealth G‑codes are, by definition, furnished remotely and therefore are paid under the same conditions as in‑person physicians' services and do not require a waiver to the requirements of section 1834(m) of the Act. Because these home telehealth services are E/M services, all other coverage and payment rules regarding E/M services continue to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telehealth home visit codes are treated as E/M services for coverage and payment; standard E/M documentation, coding, and payment policies apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telehealth cannot substitute for in‑person home health visits under HH PPS and limits on social worker telehealth
rubrics_metrics.description: Telehealth visits under the home health prospective payment system (HH PPS) cannot substitute for in‑person home health visits per section 1895(e)(1)(A) of the Act. Telehealth services by social workers cannot be furnished for CJR‑X beneficiaries who are in a home health episode because medical social services are included as home health services per section 1861(m) of the Act and paid for under the Medicare HH PPS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physicians and certain practitioners (PAs, NPs, CNSs, CNMs, nurse anesthetists, psychologists, dieticians) may furnish telehealth for beneficiaries in a home health episode, but social worker telehealth is excluded. Ensure telehealth does not supplant required in‑person HH PPS visits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Face‑to‑face encounter rules for home health certification are not relaxed by telehealth originating site waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Although sections 1835(a) and 1814(a) of the Act allow the face‑to‑face encounter to be performed via telehealth, the proposed waiver of the telehealth geographic site requirement and originating site requirement for telehealth services in the CJR‑X beneficiary's home would NOT apply to the face‑to‑face encounter required as part of home health certification when that encounter is furnished via telehealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using telehealth to meet the face‑to‑face home health certification requirement, the usual Medicare telehealth geography and originating‑site eligibility rules apply. Reminder: under §424.22(a)(1)(v) the encounter can be up to 90 days prior to start of care or within 30 days after start; certain acute/PAC physician or allowed NPP arrangements also permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions and billing rules under the proposed telehealth originating/geographic site waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the proposed waiver of the geographic site requirement and originating site requirement, all telehealth services must be furnished in accordance with all Medicare coverage and payment criteria; no additional payment would be made to cover set‑up costs, technology purchases, training and education, or other related costs; the facility fee would be waived if there is no facility as an originating site (the service originated in the beneficiary's home); providers could not bill for telehealth services that were not fully furnished when inability to provide the intended service was due to technical issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telehealth waivers apply only during the episode. Providers must not bill for services not fully delivered because of technical failures. No extra Medicare payment will be made for telehealth tech or set‑up costs; facility fee only waived when there is no originating facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring metrics for telehealth usage under CJR‑X
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS will monitor patterns of utilization of telehealth services to detect overutilization, reductions in medically necessary care, and significant reductions in face‑to‑face visits with physicians and NPPs. CMS will also monitor distribution of new telehealth home visits, anticipating greater use of lower level visits, and will monitor compliance with auxiliary staff documentation/billing rules for level 4 and 5 visits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should expect CMS evaluation of telehealth volume and mix (e.g., level distribution), face‑to‑face visit frequency, and documentation practices; improper patterns may prompt further action or policy changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNF 3‑day rule waiver eligibility: overall Five‑Star quality requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To use the SNF 3‑day rule waiver (allowing discharge to SNF after <3 inpatient days), a SNF must be rated an overall 3 stars or better by CMS's Five‑Star Quality Rating System and be included in the most recent quarter listing on Nursing Home Compare for the date of the beneficiary's admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS expects that SNFs admitting CJR‑X beneficiaries under the waiver will provide at least average overall quality. The Five‑Star system combines health inspection, staffing, and quality measures. CMS will publish the list of qualified SNFs in advance of each calendar quarter.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNF qualification rolling‑period requirement (3+ stars at least 7 of 12 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: A SNF must have been rated an overall 3 stars or better for at least 7 of the 12 months based on a review of the most recent rolling 12 months of overall star ratings to qualify under the SNF 3‑day rule waiver (unless providing SNF services under swing bed agreements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualification uses a rolling 12‑month review; swing bed providers/hospitals and CAHs under swing bed agreements are treated differently (see exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of swing bed providers and exception for providers not in Five‑Star system
rubrics_metrics.description: Providers furnishing SNF services under swing bed arrangements (hospitals or CAHs operating swing beds) may use the waiver and are not subject to the Five‑Star Quality Rating System requirement. The 3‑star/7‑of‑12‑months requirement applies only if the provider is eligible to be included in the CMS Five‑Star Quality Rating System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach preserves beneficiary choice in rural areas and aligns with prior model (TEAM) policies; CMS proposes to include swing bed providers when determining SNF qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and safeguards for SNF waiver use (patient steering and premature discharge)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS will monitor patterns of SNF utilization, particularly hospital discharge in fewer than 3 days to a SNF, to ensure beneficiaries are not discharged prematurely to SNFs and are able to exercise freedom of choice without patient steering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hospitals should expect oversight regarding discharge timing, SNF selection, and potential financial/quality impacts; CMS may act on concerning patterns identified through monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge planning notice requirement and recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X participants are required to provide a discharge planning notice to beneficiaries when using the SNF 3‑day rule waiver and to keep a record of distribution of these notices to CJR‑X beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The discharge planning notice informs beneficiaries about services, fees, and potential financial liability associated with their SNF choice. CMS will monitor use and distribution of notices and keep hospitals financially responsible when notices are not provided as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial liability assignment when SNF waiver is used inappropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: If a CJR‑X participant discharges a beneficiary without a qualifying 3‑day inpatient stay to a SNF that is not on the published list of qualified SNFs at the date of admission, then: (a) if the participant failed to provide the required discharge planning notice, the CJR‑X participant will be financially liable for the SNF stay; (b) if the participant provided the notice and the beneficiary chose the non‑qualified SNF, the beneficiary assumes financial liability for services furnished (except Part B covered services during a non‑covered inpatient SNF stay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes that when hospitals fail to provide required notices they bear ultimate financial responsibility; when notice is provided, beneficiaries who choose non‑qualified SNFs accept liability. This mirrors prior CJR policy to place financial risk for misuse on participant hospitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS remedial rules when hospital fails to provide discharge planning notice
rubrics_metrics.description: If a beneficiary is discharged to a SNF without a qualifying 3‑day inpatient stay, the SNF is not on the qualified list as of admission date, and the hospital failed to provide the discharge planning notice, CMS proposes: (1) CMS does not make payment to the SNF for such services; (2) the SNF must not charge the beneficiary for expenses and must return any monies collected; and (3) the hospital must be responsible for the cost of the uncovered SNF stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These remedial rules are proposed to protect beneficiaries from financial liability caused by inappropriate use of the waiver and hospital noncompliance with notice requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to share beneficiary‑identifiable claims data with CJR‑X participants under HIPAA and the Privacy Act
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS asserts that sharing beneficiary‑identifiable claims data with CJR‑X hospital participants for evaluating performance, quality assessment/improvement, population‑based activities, and health care operations is permissible under the HIPAA Privacy Rule (45 CFR 164.506(c)(4)) and consistent with Privacy Act routine uses (DERS system of records).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures will be to HIPAA covered entities (hospitals bearing risk) that have or had a relationship with the subject and will use the data for permitted health care operations. Comment requested on these authority assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum necessary and limiting scope of beneficiary‑identifiable data shared
rubrics_metrics.description: When using or disclosing PHI, covered entities must apply 'reasonable efforts to limit' information to the 'minimum necessary' to accomplish the intended purpose (45 CFR 164.502(b)). CMS believes the proposed data elements constitute the minimum necessary for CJR‑X goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will limit shared data to items and services included in the episode and to beneficiaries who initiated an episode at the hospital; data will not include unrelated services before/after the episode (e.g., primary care visit five days before episode).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal and population limits on claims data (3‑year baseline and monthly reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to offer beneficiary‑identifiable claims data for a 3‑year baseline period (only for beneficiaries who initiated an episode at the hospital during baseline) and on a monthly basis during the performance year, limited to items and services included in the episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline data limited to episode initiators at the hospital; no claims for beneficiaries who did not initiate an episode at that hospital; similar approach for performance year monthly data to enable care coordination and performance assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients limited to hospitals bearing financial risk; hospitals responsible for re‑disclosure decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to disclose beneficiary‑identifiable data only to the hospitals that are bearing risk for episodes and not to their collaborators. The hospitals that are financially responsible should determine which data to re‑disclose to collaborators, consistent with HIPAA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CJR‑X participant hospitals must manage downstream disclosures and ensure any re‑disclosures comply with HIPAA health care operations rules and minimum necessary requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two data formats offered: summary beneficiary‑identifiable claims data and raw beneficiary‑identifiable claims data
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to make claims data available in two formats: summary (aggregated/categorized to provide a broad view of participant's expenditures and utilization) and raw (unrefined, episode‑level claims fields as described in minimum necessary section, including episode summaries, indicators for excluded episodes, diagnosis/procedure codes, enrollment and dual eligibility info).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary data can reveal patterns (e.g., high readmission rates for a provider) to guide quality improvement; raw data allows case‑level analysis (e.g., diagnoses associated with readmission). Participants must enter into a data sharing agreement to request either format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing agreement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR‑X participants must enter into a CJR‑X data sharing agreement with CMS (specified in the proposed rule) to request and receive summary or raw beneficiary‑identifiable claims data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agreement will set privacy, security, and permissible use conditions; only participants who execute the agreement may request data.
